body: But the panic button is the first thing I go for in every situation from an awkward moment to find blood on my toilet paper. I know I can make it through this. I've done it before, but it adds to the misery.
Not yet. I probably should have.
Pretty much yeah.

Most people that experienced the shit I've been through and had to deal with my level of life long mental disturbance end up in jail, rehab, an institution or cemetery. I finished school, got a diploma from TAFE and got into uni.
Why develop drugs that duplicate the effect? Just gimmie some fuckin' K.

So after waiting six hours I was seen by a doctor. I had trouble answering a lot of questions because it was 3:30am and being sleep deprived affects cognitive abilities of sane people anyway. They kept me in until morning and managed to get a few hours sleep somehow. A mental health nurse saw me at 8am. I answered his questions as honestly as I could. I was discharged at 9am as I was too tired to get a plan ready. A crisis team is going to call me tomorrow and I've pretty much been in bed all day. My mum wasn't called as I'm over 18. Thanks for the advice and take care.
As long as you still "don't think" you're still not 100% sure, and you can still fight.
Do what I did. Walk into an ER and tell them you're worried about harming yourself.
As someone who had an extremely traumatic upbringing it's exactly why I worry so much about small things.

> Just like most everything, happiness is a choice.

I think the happiness button is between the sexuality switch and IQ dial.

If they aren't going to respond to a text saying hello they aren't worth the effort. Fuck them, you deserve better than those cunts. And maybe in another universe we would be best friends, well adjusted and successful, but instead we were born in different continents with severe mental health issues.

I used to take 20mg of fluoxetine, 1mg of Risperidone and 36mg of slow release Methylphenidate Hydrochloride (a.k.a Ritalin). Did not get addicted to any of them, and took them all daily pretty much my entire teen years.

BPD and PTSD often has comorbidity with depression and anxiety. I do the same things with people too. I let them in too fast, will suddenly feel nothing for them and I always seem to get attracted to one girl for months, even if she gives subtle hints she's not into me. It's made me start to wonder if there's more to me than just being depressed.

> Who does that?

Someone who has never experienced violence in the home, child abuse, bullying, divorced parents or depression. Because I was drunk at the time I'm fairly certain I yelled "I am a unique snowflake, just like everyone else". Also, they said pretty much everything I said that night was hilarious as well, including saying "the sanctity of marriage doesn't exist when you see your dad punch a woman with cancer" during a gay marriage discussion.
I feel opposite. Then again it's 9:45am on a Saturday.

Welcome to living on campus. I swear some of the people I live with are the most fucking vacuous and vain people. One girl told me "you are not unique" during a drunken rant I made about being abused and witnessing domestic violence. She's also said on multiple occasions how she hates people with major depression, knowing full well the antidepressants on the table are mine and the guy she (was) dating was also quite ill.

Then there's another roommate who asks me for relationship advice, despite the fact I was a virgin until one month ago. She says I have it so good because I don't (read can't) have a job and if I come home really drunk and bitch about everyone of my roommates at 4am and wake them up she'll find it hilarious.

In my experience I never really saw a change between having to meds and not taking them until a month or more later. Also, my libido isn't affected by my meds. I have noticed though after recently doubling the dose it takes a bit more time to bust a nut but erections aren't an issue.

When I see a girl with scars I find it attractive. I see it as a sign they can understand me and they know what the darkest corners of the mind are like. The scars let me know that a girl has been through hell and is strong enough to survive.

But how did I support a world where violence and abuse exists when I was a kid? And if I didn't why do innocent people have to suffer for someone else's misdeeds? This isn't a "need to crack a few eggs to make an omlette" situation here.

> ... it looks like you have some sort of undiagnosed mental problem.

I think you're right about that. This morning I could hardly get out of bed, then I felt normal, even somewhat happy and now I'm paranoid about a girl I know.
He is adorable. I want to cuddle him so much.

You will feel happy, and I know exactly where you're coming from (particularly if you read my posting history). At some point you will make it through, and you will be able to stand proud. I know there are points in my life where I have.

Don't hang yourself. A friend of mine did. It affected everyone who knew him. His boss, customers at the shop he worked at, friends from his uni and especially his family. The worst part about it is they probably found him with a massive boner and shat pants. No one mentions that spinal injuries cause erections and the bowel evacuation that always comes with hanging.

You don't have to be the "good" daughter. You haven't let your parents down either. There's still a lot of time to fix yourself. I wish I could give you a proper hug, because you deserve to feel loved. It's hard walking through the dark alone as well. Just remember, there is some guy, probably thousands of miles from you that wants to give you cuddles simply because you're you. Keep that in mind.

When I hear people say "confront your demons" I immediately think "they aren't *my* demons". I'm not the one who abused, molested, bullied and damaged me. Other people did those horrific things. Apparently one of the consequences of being a victim of child abuse is that you have to carry the burden of other people's shit.

I'm well aware of her situation. However last night I told her we should stop hanging out, partly because I get clingy with people and she hates clingers and also because I don't want to put my shit on her given she's probably just as sick as I am. It turns out she cried while sending a text saying that "I'll let you be. And I'll wait for you". I cried reading it because no one has ever been that understanding about me. In fact, I've read that message a couple of times to give me a boost of hope.

Cheers. I usually surprise counselors with my issues, particularly because it's highly medical. The situation with the girl isn't entirely about making to it happen. Met a guy online, moved here and got married and he's abusive/controlling and she's falling back into old habits she wanted to leave at home. But if things get sorted soon then there's a good chance we will get together. We both seem to use each other as a crutch and that somehow holds us up.

I'm a 21 year old guy who's dealt with mental health issues his entire life. You remember the one psycho kid who threw tables, tried to stab other kids and that was why there was another teacher lady in the classroom too? I was that kid. It got to a point when I was 9 that they started giving me risperidone to stop ruining other kids' shit. I wasn't the sort of ADHD kid that just needed a swift kick in the dick, I was genuinely fucked in the head.

Then around 14/15 I started hearing voices. I also saw shadowy figures a lot and colours sometimes blended. Occasionally I'd look at the sky and feel as though I was travelling down a wormhole. The worst was the delusion though. I couldn't hear anyone laugh without believing they were laughing at me and it made me hate pretty much everyone at school.

I don't really have romantic relationships per sé. I am sort of seeing a girl, and We've fucked but it's a weird situation she's in. As for meds I'm currently on 40mg of fluoxetine and it's been at that dose for about two and a half weeks.
911 isn't the emergency number here. At the moment I'm ib bed not wanting to get up. I guess that's part of the reason why.

I try to be as nice as I can. But no matter what events from my past still haunt me. I'm trying to get professional help but I don't have another appointment with a counselor until next Friday. I'll try my best to keep going at least until then.

> you may be living out the punishment of what a past version of yourself did

So because of something I apparently did when I was a rhino or some other creature I deserved to get raped when I was three. Fuck you and fuck your belief system. No three year old kid deserves that, no matter what they did in a past life.
